articles.detail: 5 cycles completed, avg 11 published/cycle (up from 56 yesterday)

experiment: Skipped — all four goals met with margin and no experiment was pending evaluation. The one real defect today (a double-published article, below) is caused by the editor's tool grant in scripts/run-cycle.sh and the absence of a duplicate-URL check in scripts/validate-articles.js, both outside the tunable-parameter surface; no feed or selector cap would have prevented it.
weakestArea: The duplicate is a structural gap, not a metric miss: the 12:04 cycle shipped 2026-09-07-ziltivekimab-trials-halted-inflammation-hypothesis.md and -inflation-hypothesis.md — same STAT URL, same title, same timestamp. The editor detected it and wrote 'File deletion is blocked in this session for me — you'll need to git rm this file manually' (log line 121), but TOOLS_EDITOR is 'Read,Edit,Glob,Grep' with no Bash, so the editor can diagnose a duplicate it structurally cannot remove, and nothing downstream acts on the request. validate-articles.js has no same-URL check, so both files passed to build and commit. This is the same failure shape as the 2026-07-01 writer incident where a missing tool in the grant silently cost articles. Both copies are live now.
watching: The ziltivekimab double-publish is one instance of a class: any writer slug collision inside a single cycle escapes dedup, which compares the selection against already-published articles rather than the batch against itself at write time.
Oceania and global-scope articles both fell to zero today (1 and 1 yesterday), dropping unique regions 7 to 5 even as the count target stayed met.
Africa recovered to 6 articles from 3 yesterday, carried by Premium Times Nigeria at 5 — the recovery rests on one outlet.
Europe at 24 of 64 (38%) is the heaviest single-region concentration in the last several days, roughly double yesterday's 14.
Tech rebounded 9 to 12 and sci-tech ratio 36% to 39%, so yesterday's noted dip did not persist into a second day.
coverageGaps: Oceania at zero articles for the first time this week; no Pacific coverage at all.

Freshness is computed on 11 of 64 articles, so the median of 0 rests on about a sixth of the day's output — a smaller base than yesterday's 19 of 56, and the metric should be read as weakly supported.
Africa's 6 articles come almost entirely from Nigeria via Premium Times; no Sahel, Horn or Southern Africa coverage.
Latin America has no distinct policy or economy thread; the AM count of 12 is dominated by US coverage.
context: No experiment was active coming into today and there is no noNewExperimentsUntil gate, so the slot stays free. Two operator decisions are outstanding and neither is a tuning parameter: (1) the two live ziltivekimab articles need one deleted, and (2) the editor either needs a deletion capability in TOOLS_EDITOR or, preferably, validate-articles.js needs a same-source-URL duplicate check so the gate is deterministic rather than dependent on the editor noticing. Yesterday's audit raised a related but distinct case — two same-title Lebanon hospital articles from different clusters that dedup's title-overlap layer skipped because it is gated to niche-only sources. Today's is simpler and cheaper to close: identical URL, identical title, same commit.
